news.content: 站内 全人群普遍易感!内蒙古疾控中心发布风险提示 城市速递 2026年11月12日 11:28:57 来自北京市 据内蒙古疾控消息,诺如病毒胃肠炎是由诺如病毒(Norovirus,NoV)感染引起的急性消化道传染病,具有高度传染性和快速传播能力。诺如病毒具有多个基因型,其中GI和GII是引起人类感染性腹泻的两个主要基因组。 诺如病毒变异快、免疫保护时间短。同一个人可重复感染同一毒株或不同型别的诺如病毒,不同基因型之间无交叉免疫。诺如病毒具有传染性强、感染剂量低、排毒时间长、免疫保护时间短和全人群普遍易感等特点。主要通过病人的粪便和呕吐物排出,隐性感染者也可排毒。病人在潜伏期即可排出诺如病毒,排毒高峰在发病后2-5天,持续约2-3周。 感染诺如病毒的病人及隐性感染者均为诺如病毒感染的传染源。诺如病毒传播途径多样,接触感染诺如病毒的病人,比如处理病人的呕吐物或排泄物,通过摄入粪便或呕吐物产生的气溶胶或间接接触被排泄物污染的环境传播;也可通过食用和饮用被病毒污染的食物和水传播。 诺如病毒对环境抵抗力强,在0-60°C的温度范围内均可存活,可在物体表面存活2周,在水中存活2个月以上。 酒精和免冲洗洗手液没有灭活效果,但使用较高浓度含氯消毒剂(处理污水1小时后余氯浓度大于10mg/L)可灭活诺如病毒。主要防护建议1.保持良好的手卫生。保持良好的手卫生是预防诺如病毒感染和控制诺如病毒传播最重要和最有效的措施。饭前、便后、加工食物前应按照6步洗手法正确洗手,用肥皂和流动水至少洗20秒。2.注意个人饮食卫生。喝开水,蔬菜瓜果彻底洗净,烹饪食物要煮熟,尤其是贝类等海鲜类食品更要煮熟煮透。3.做好消毒工作。对患者呕吐物或粪便污染的环境和物品需要使用含氯制剂进行消毒。在清理受到呕吐物污染的物品时,应戴塑胶手套和口罩,避免直接接触污染物。患者家庭环境也应根据医务人员指导加强消毒,避免在家庭内造成传播。4.托幼机构和学校等集体单位应做好宣传。做好诺如病毒感染的健康教育工作,倡导良好的卫生习惯和饮食习惯,倡导学生积极锻炼身体,提高免疫力。 送你新闻盲盒 选一个拆开吧 来源 丨内蒙古疾控 编辑丨张国军 值班主任丨格根哈斯 审核丨王雪仙 张群群 李涛 点亮“ ”和“ ” 给小布加个鸡腿吧 本文来自大风号,仅代表大风号自媒体观点。 凤凰V现场 独家对话深蓝CEO姜海荣:大模型上车,车机正在告别“听指令” 德国IFA直击:中国企业如何用AI读懂一个家?2026中国联通合作伙伴大会在上海举行,九大成果看联通智能化布局华为Mate XT 2展翼三折叠深度体验:三折叠的新答案IFA 2026 ,安克硬控全场查看更多

news.content_original: 站内 全人群普遍易感!内蒙古疾控中心发布风险提示 城市速递 2026年11月12日 11:28:57 来自北京市 据内蒙古疾控消息,诺如病毒胃肠炎是由诺如病毒(Norovirus,NoV)感染引起的急性消化道传染病,具有高度传染性和快速传播能力。诺如病毒具有多个基因型,其中GI和GII是引起人类感染性腹泻的两个主要基因组。 诺如病毒变异快、免疫保护时间短。同一个人可重复感染同一毒株或不同型别的诺如病毒,不同基因型之间无交叉免疫。诺如病毒具有传染性强、感染剂量低、排毒时间长、免疫保护时间短和全人群普遍易感等特点。主要通过病人的粪便和呕吐物排出,隐性感染者也可排毒。病人在潜伏期即可排出诺如病毒,排毒高峰在发病后2-5天,持续约2-3周。 感染诺如病毒的病人及隐性感染者均为诺如病毒感染的传染源。诺如病毒传播途径多样,接触感染诺如病毒的病人,比如处理病人的呕吐物或排泄物,通过摄入粪便或呕吐物产生的气溶胶或间接接触被排泄物污染的环境传播;也可通过食用和饮用被病毒污染的食物和水传播。 诺如病毒对环境抵抗力强,在0-60°C的温度范围内均可存活,可在物体表面存活2周,在水中存活2个月以上。 酒精和免冲洗洗手液没有灭活效果,但使用较高浓度含氯消毒剂(处理污水1小时后余氯浓度大于10mg/L)可灭活诺如病毒。主要防护建议1.保持良好的手卫生。保持良好的手卫生是预防诺如病毒感染和控制诺如病毒传播最重要和最有效的措施。饭前、便后、加工食物前应按照6步洗手法正确洗手,用肥皂和流动水至少洗20秒。2.注意个人饮食卫生。喝开水,蔬菜瓜果彻底洗净,烹饪食物要煮熟,尤其是贝类等海鲜类食品更要煮熟煮透。3.做好消毒工作。对患者呕吐物或粪便污染的环境和物品需要使用含氯制剂进行消毒。在清理受到呕吐物污染的物品时,应戴塑胶手套和口罩,避免直接接触污染物。患者家庭环境也应根据医务人员指导加强消毒,避免在家庭内造成传播。4.托幼机构和学校等集体单位应做好宣传。做好诺如病毒感染的健康教育工作,倡导良好的卫生习惯和饮食习惯,倡导学生积极锻炼身体,提高免疫力。 送你新闻盲盒 选一个拆开吧 来源 丨内蒙古疾控 编辑丨张国军 值班主任丨格根哈斯 审核丨王雪仙 张群群 李涛 点亮“ ”和“ ” 给小布加个鸡腿吧 本文来自大风号,仅代表大风号自媒体观点。 凤凰V现场 独家对话深蓝CEO姜海荣:大模型上车,车机正在告别“听指令” 德国IFA直击:中国企业如何用AI读懂一个家?2026中国联通合作伙伴大会在上海举行,九大成果看联通智能化布局华为Mate XT 2展翼三折叠深度体验:三折叠的新答案IFA 2026 ,安克硬控全场查看更多

news.content_title: 又一款疫苗3期失利
news.content: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 又一款疫苗3期失利 2026-11-16 09:58 来源: 药智网搜狐号 发布于:重庆市 近期,Moderna在第三季度财报及电话会上披露,其旗下诺如病毒疫苗mRNA-1403的III期临床试验中期分析未达到提前成功的统计学标准。经过重新评估,Moderna决定不再于即将到来的冬季新增研究队列,而是与监管机构讨论后续开发路径。 这一决定不仅使疫苗后续的有效性验证面临新的挑战,也为其未来的上市进程增添了不确定性。 1. 诺如病毒疫苗III期临床受挫 Moderna作为mRNA疗法先驱,其业务覆盖传染病疫苗、肿瘤治疗及罕见病等多个领域。凭借新冠疫苗Spikevax的商业化成功,Moderna持续拓展mRNA技术的应用范围,先后布局呼吸道合胞病毒、流感、巨细胞病毒及诺如病毒等多个疫苗项目。其中,mRNA-1403是其已推进至临床III期的诺如病毒疫苗候选产品。 诺如病毒是全球急性胃肠炎的重要病原体之一,具有传染性强、传播途径广、感染剂量低等特点。感染者通常会引起腹泻、呕吐、恶心及腹痛等症状,多数患者可在数日内自行恢复,但婴幼儿、老年人及免疫功能低下者可能因严重脱水而住院,甚至危及生命。据WHO数据显示,全球每年约发生6.85亿例诺如病毒感染病例,导致约20万人死亡,造成疾病相关医疗成本与经济损失合计约600亿美元。 目前,诺如病毒感染的预防仍主要依赖个人卫生、环境消毒及感染控制措施,尚无获批上市的针对性疫苗或特效药物。庞大的疾病负担与尚未满足的预防需求,使诺如病毒疫苗成为具有较大开发潜力的领域。然而,该病毒具有广泛的遗传多样性,不同基因群及基因型之间存在抗原差异,单一毒株疫苗难以覆盖全部流行类型,因此,多价疫苗成为当前主要研发思路之一。 Moderna开发的mRNA-1403是一款三价mRNA疫苗,通过脂质纳米颗粒递送编码诺如病毒主要衣壳蛋白VP1的mRNA(图1),覆盖GI.3、GII.3及GII.4三种基因型,旨在诱导机体产生针对相关病毒抗原的免疫反应。与通过体外生产病毒样颗粒的传统技术路线不同,mRNA平台利用人体细胞表达目标抗原,在疫苗抗原组合设计与生产方面具有一定灵活性。 图1 mRNA-1403三价诺如病毒疫苗作用机制示意图 图片来源:Moderna官网 展开全文 早期研究曾为mRNA-1403提供积极信号。2024年,Moderna公布的I/II期研究数据显示,单剂mRNA-1403在所评估剂量下总体耐受性良好,并可诱导针对疫苗匹配基因型的抗体反应,包括具有功能意义的组织血型抗原(HBGA)阻断抗体。基于早期研究结果,Moderna于2024年9月正式启动关键III期Nova 301试验,进一步验证疫苗预防实际疾病的效果。 但mRNA-1403的后期开发并不顺利。2025年2月,Moderna披露,由于试验中报告了一例格林-巴利综合征(GBS)不良事件,美国FDA对该研究实施临床暂停。2025Q1,相关临床暂停措施被解除,研究得以继续推进。 今年7月31日,Moderna在第二季度财报中正式确认,mRNA-1403的III期中期分析未达到提前成功的统计学标准。不过,公司同时强调研究仍在进行且保持盲态,并准备通过增加研究队列继续积累病例。 然而,据Moderna在11月6日公布的第三季度财报显示,其已经决定不再于本轮冬季招募新增队列,而是先与监管机构讨论项目的下一步安排。 从2024年启动III期临床到今年中期分析未达标、原定新增队列被取消,mRNA-1403的研发进程已经明显偏离最初预期。 2. III期临床试验未达预期背后 mRNA-1403的关键III期研究Nova 301(NCT06592794)是一项随机、观察者盲法、安慰剂对照的III期研究(图2)。受试者按研究方案接受单剂mRNA-1403或安慰剂,通过后续随访比较两组发生诺如病毒相关急性胃肠炎的情况以评价疫苗的保护效力及安全性。研究的主要终点是评估mRNA-1403预防疫苗所覆盖基因型引起的中重度诺如病毒急性胃肠炎的保护效力。 图2 mRNA-1403关键III期Nova 301初始临床试验设计 图片来源:Moderna官网 需要注意的是,并非研究期间发生的所有诺如病毒感染都能计入主要终点。只有病毒基因型和疾病严重程度等符合预设标准的病例,才能纳入主要终点分析。因此,除了疫苗本身的保护效果,符合条件的感染病例数量也是影响研究统计结果的重要因素。 2026年7月,Moderna确认mRNA-1403的III期中期分析未达到预设的提前成功标准。不过,公司尚未公布具体的疫苗保护效力、置信区间及两组主要终点病例数量。因此,当前尚无法判断疫苗的实际保护效果,也不能将中期分析未达标直接等同于疫苗保护效力不足。 对于研究进展不及预期,Moderna此前披露了一个重要影响因素,即实际流行的诺如病毒毒株与研究主要终点所覆盖的基因型存在差异。在2026年第二季度财报电话会上,Moderna总裁Stephen Hoge表示,Nova 301第一个流行季出现了不同诺如病毒毒株的异常流行,部分感染病例未能计入主要终点,导致符合条件的病例积累慢于预期,中期分析时间也因此有所推迟。 为进一步积累有效病例、增强最终分析的统计学证据,Moderna原计划继续扩大研究。Hoge在第二季度财报电话会上表示,公司准备进入第三个冬季研究阶段,通过招募更多受试者积累感染病例,为最终有效性分析提供更多数据支持。不过,跨流行季开展研究不仅会延长开发周期、增加临床试验成本,还可能面临优势流行毒株再次变化的问题。因此,即使增加研究队列,能否获得足够的有效病例并达到预设的统计学标准,仍存在不确定性。 3. mRNA-1403开发前景及行业启示 11月6日,在第三季度财报电话会上,Moderna总裁Stephen Hoge表示,经过重新评估,公司决定不再于即将到来的冬季新增研究队列,而是先与监管机构沟通再确定后续开发方案。这一决定意味着Moderna已对mRNA-1403原定的临床开发计划作出调整。 值得注意的是,Hoge并未披露促使公司改变计划的具体原因。因此,目前尚不能将取消新增队列直接视为III期临床试验最终失败。 从公司层面看,mRNA-1403开发前景的不确定性增加,恰逢Moderna持续优化研发投入的背景下。 据Moderna 2026年第三季度财报显示,公司研发费用为5.83亿美元,同比下降27%(图3),主要与部分传染病后期临床研究完成以及持续推进成本控制有关。这表明Moderna正更加重视研发资源的合理配置。对于需要跨多个流行季开展的大型疫苗临床试验,新增研究队列不仅意味着延长开发周期,还将增加临床研究成本。 因此,在现有数据尚不足以支持提前成功判断的情况下,继续扩大试验规模的投入产出是否合理,也可能成为公司重新评估项目的重要考量。不过,Moderna尚未明确将此次决策调整归因于成本因素。 图3 Moderna 2026年Q3财报数据 图片来源:Moderna官网 与此同时,Moderna其他后期研发管线仍在推进。今年8月,其季节性流感疫苗mFLUSIVA获得FDA批准,流感与新冠联合疫苗mRNA-1083也已在欧洲和加拿大获得相关监管批准。在肿瘤领域,Moderna与默沙东合作开发的个体化肿瘤治疗产品intismeran autogene(mRNA-4157)在III期INTerpath-001研究中取得积极结果。 由此可见,Moderna已拥有商业化产品及多条处于不同开发阶段的研发管线。mRNA-1403的研发受挫更多影响的是其在诺如病毒疫苗领域的布局及潜在商业化机会,尚不足以对其整体业务构成根本性冲击。 事实上,诺如病毒疫苗研发受挫并非个例。2024年7月8日,HilleVax公布旗下诺如病毒疫苗HIL-214的IIb期临床结果。在NEST-IN1研究中,共有51起主要终点事件,其中疫苗组25起(n=1425),安慰剂组26起(n=1399),疫苗效力仅为5%,研究未达到主要终点。随后,HilleVax宣布停止该疫苗在婴幼儿人群中的进一步开发。受此消息影响,Hillevax股价暴跌88.34%,总市值8154.32万美元。 尽管HIL-214采用病毒样颗粒技术,与Moderna的mRNA技术路线不同,且两项研究的目标人群和试验设计存在差异,但这些研发挫折也反映出诺如病毒疫苗临床开发的复杂性。 4. 结语 截至目前,mRNA-1403的最终命运仍未确定。但Moderna取消新增队列、优先与监管机构沟通已经表明该项目的后续开发存在较大不确定性。 从行业角度来看,mRNA-1403事件再次说明疫苗早期免疫原性表现与III期临床保护效力之间始终存在需要通过大规模试验验证的距离。即便技术平台已获得商业化验证,单个产品的成功仍取决于其能否获得足够可靠且符合监管要求的有效性证据。 参考资料 [1]https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06592794 为进一步积累有效病例、增强最终分析的统计学证据,Moderna原计划继续扩大研究。Hoge在第二季度财报电话会上表示,公司准备进入第三个冬季研究阶段,通过招募更多受试者积累感染病例,为最终有效性分析提供更多数据支持。不过,跨流行季开展研究不仅会延长开发周期、增加临床试验成本,还可能面临优势流行毒株再次变化的问题。因此,即使增加研究队列,能否获得足够的有效病例并达到预设的统计学标准,仍存在不确定性。 3. mRNA-1403开发前景及行业启示 11月6日,在第三季度财报电话会上,Moderna总裁Stephen Hoge表示,经过重新评估,公司决定不再于即将到来的冬季新增研究队列,而是先与监管机构沟通再确定后续开发方案。这一决定意味着Moderna已对mRNA-1403原定的临床开发计划作出调整。 值得注意的是,Hoge并未披露促使公司改变计划的具体原因。因此,目前尚不能将取消新增队列直接视为III期临床试验最终失败。 从公司层面看,mRNA-1403开发前景的不确定性增加,恰逢Moderna持续优化研发投入的背景下。 据Moderna 2026年第三季度财报显示,公司研发费用为5.83亿美元,同比下降27%(图3),主要与部分传染病后期临床研究完成以及持续推进成本控制有关。这表明Moderna正更加重视研发资源的合理配置。对于需要跨多个流行季开展的大型疫苗临床试验,新增研究队列不仅意味着延长开发周期,还将增加临床研究成本。 因此,在现有数据尚不足以支持提前成功判断的情况下,继续扩大试验规模的投入产出是否合理,也可能成为公司重新评估项目的重要考量。不过,Moderna尚未明确将此次决策调整归因于成本因素。 图3 Moderna 2026年Q3财报数据 图片来源:Moderna官网 与此同时,Moderna其他后期研发管线仍在推进。今年8月,其季节性流感疫苗mFLUSIVA获得FDA批准,流感与新冠联合疫苗mRNA-1083也已在欧洲和加拿大获得相关监管批准。在肿瘤领域,Moderna与默沙东合作开发的个体化肿瘤治疗产品intismeran autogene(mRNA-4157)在III期INTerpath-001研究中取得积极结果。 由此可见,Moderna已拥有商业化产品及多条处于不同开发阶段的研发管线。mRNA-1403的研发受挫更多影响的是其在诺如病毒疫苗领域的布局及潜在商业化机会,尚不足以对其整体业务构成根本性冲击。 事实上,诺如病毒疫苗研发受挫并非个例。2024年7月8日,HilleVax公布旗下诺如病毒疫苗HIL-214的IIb期临床结果。在NEST-IN1研究中,共有51起主要终点事件,其中疫苗组25起(n=1425),安慰剂组26起(n=1399),疫苗效力仅为5%,研究未达到主要终点。随后,HilleVax宣布停止该疫苗在婴幼儿人群中的进一步开发。受此消息影响,Hillevax股价暴跌88.34%,总市值8154.32万美元。 尽管HIL-214采用病毒样颗粒技术,与Moderna的mRNA技术路线不同,且两项研究的目标人群和试验设计存在差异,但这些研发挫折也反映出诺如病毒疫苗临床开发的复杂性。 4. 结语 截至目前,mRNA-1403的最终命运仍未确定。但Moderna取消新增队列、优先与监管机构沟通已经表明该项目的后续开发存在较大不确定性。 从行业角度来看,mRNA-1403事件再次说明疫苗早期免疫原性表现与III期临床保护效力之间始终存在需要通过大规模试验验证的距离。即便技术平台已获得商业化验证,单个产品的成功仍取决于其能否获得足够可靠且符合监管要求的有效性证据。 参考资料 [1]https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06592794 source_language_evidence.time: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 又一款疫苗3期失利 2026-11-16 09:58 来源: 药智网搜狐号 发布于:重庆市 近期,Moderna在第三季度财报及电话会上披露,其旗下诺如病毒疫苗mRNA-1403的III期临床试验中期分析未达到提前成功的统计学标准。经过重新评估,Moderna决定不再于即将到来的冬季新增研究队列,而是与监管机构讨论后续开发路径。
source_language_evidence.event: 这一决定不仅使疫苗后续的有效性验证面临新的挑战,也为其未来的上市进程增添了不确定性。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: III期临床试验未达预期背后 mRNA-1403的关键III期研究Nova 301(NCT06592794)是一项随机、观察者盲法、安慰剂对照的III期研究(图2)。受试者按研究方案接受单剂mRNA-1403或安慰剂,通过后续随访比较两组发生诺如病毒相关急性胃肠炎的情况以评价疫苗的保护效力及安全性。研究的主要终点是评估mRNA-1403预防疫苗所覆盖基因型引起的中重度诺如病毒急性胃肠炎的保护效力。
source_language_evidence.brief_en: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 又一款疫苗3期失利 2026-11-16 09:58 来源: 药智网搜狐号 发布于:重庆市 近期,Moderna在第三季度财报及电话会上披露,其旗下诺如病毒疫苗mRNA-1403的III期临床试验中期分析未达到提前成功的统计学标准。经过重新评估,Moderna决定不再于即将到来的冬季新增研究队列,而是与监管机构讨论后续开发路径。 这一决定不仅使疫苗后续的有效性验证面临新的挑战,也为其未来的上市进程增添了不确定性。 诺如病毒疫苗III期临床受挫 Moderna作为mRNA疗法先驱,其业务覆盖传染病疫苗、肿瘤治疗及罕见病等多个领域。凭借新冠疫苗Spikevax的商业化成功,Moderna持续拓展mRNA技术的应用范围,先后布局呼吸道合胞病毒、流感、巨细胞病毒及诺如病毒等多个疫苗项目。其中,mRNA-1403是其已推进至临床III期的诺如病毒疫苗候选产品。 诺如病毒是全球急性胃肠炎的重要病原体之一,具有传染性强、传播途径广、感染剂量低等特点。感染者通常会引起腹泻、呕吐、恶心及腹痛等症状,多数患者可在数日内自行恢复,但婴幼儿、老年人及免疫功能低下者可能因严重脱水而住院,甚至危及生命。据WHO数据显示,全球每年约发生6.85亿例诺如病毒感染病例,导致约20万人死亡,造成疾病相关医疗成本与经济损失合计约600亿美元。 目前,诺如病毒感染的预防仍主要依赖个人卫生、环境消毒及感染控制措施,尚无获批上市的针对性疫苗或特效药物。庞大的疾病负担与尚未满足的预防需求,使诺如病毒疫苗成为具有较大开发潜力的领域。然而,该病毒具有广泛的遗传多样性,不同基因群及基因型之间存在抗原差异,单一毒株疫苗难以覆盖全部流行类型,因此,多价疫苗成为当前主要研发思路之一。 Moderna开发的mRNA-1403是一款三价mRNA疫苗,通过脂质纳米颗粒递送编码诺如病毒主要衣壳蛋白VP1的mRNA(图1),覆盖GI.3、GII.3及GII.4三种基因型,旨在诱导机体产生针对相关病毒抗原的免疫反应。与通过体外生产病毒样颗粒的传统技术路线不同,mRNA平台利用人体细胞表达目标抗原,在疫苗抗原组合设计与生产方面具有一定灵活性。 图1 mRNA-1403三价诺如病毒疫苗作用机制示意图 图片来源:Moderna官网 展开全文 早期研究曾为mRNA-1403提供积极信号。2024年,Moderna公布的I/II期研究数据显示,单剂mRNA-1403在所评估剂量下总体耐受性良好,并可诱导针对疫苗匹配基因型的抗体反应,包括具有功能意义的组织血型抗原(HBGA)阻断抗体。基于早期研究结果,Moderna于2024年9月正式启动关键III期Nova 301试验,进一步验证疫苗预防实际疾病的效果。

Add to preferred sources News Elaine Blackburne and Jordan Coussins 11:01, 14 Nov 2026Updated 12:50, 14 Nov 2026 Key 'American Covid' advice as Brits told 'stay at home' in six-symptom message(Image: Getty) Health authorities have issued an urgent warning as cases of a debilitating illness continue to climb. Members of the public are being advised to remain at home for 48 hours should they develop certain key symptoms of the infection — and cautioned that hand sanitiser will not be effective against it. Article continues below Powered By Hearts v Hibs - Premier Sports Cup match preview Share Next Stay In a post on X, formerly Twitter, the UKHSA has flagged that the number of people contracting norovirus has risen recently. It reports a total of 2,111 laboratory-confirmed cases of the infection so far during the current season — a rise of 16.8% on the five-season average for the equivalent period. Article continues below MDs: The Boxed Cereal Seniors Ask About Most When Memory Comes UpMemory Health Journal | SponsoredSponsored While figures remain within anticipated levels, the agency has alerted the public that infections have started to increase, with 257 reported cases over the fortnight up to last week. It has also provided guidance on the steps people should take should they experience any symptoms of the bug. Norovirus is commonly known as the winter vomiting bug, despite being contractable at any time of year. It is a stomach illness that triggers vomiting and diarrhoea, spreading rapidly through communities and making outbreaks particularly prevalent in environments where people are in close proximity, such as hospitals, care homes, cruise ships, schools and nurseries. Get breaking news on BirminghamLive WhatsApp, click the link to join Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Article continues below Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings. The virus targets the stomach and intestines, and is alternatively referred to as a gastrointestinal virus, gastric flu or a stomach bug. You can contract norovirus multiple times within a brief period because various types (or genotypes) of norovirus are in circulation at any moment, and while you may build limited immunity to one strain, you can still be infected by another variant shortly afterwards, reports the Mirror. Article continues below The UKHSA previously cautioned: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop as you are still infectious during this time." It also highlighted at the time that hand sanitiser will not work to prevent the illness. To stop the virus spreading, the health service advises those displaying symptoms should refrain from attending school, work, hospitals, and care homes until 48 hours following the cessation of symptoms. Beyond self-isolating while unwell, the NHS outlines several measures to curb the infection's transmission, recommending that you should:. Should you display any symptoms, the health body suggests:. Article continues below If you or your child experience diarrhoea for longer than seven days or vomiting for beyond two days, you should ring 111. According to the NHS, norovirus symptoms can emerge "suddenly" and typically comprise nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea. It states: "It can be very unpleasant, but usually gets better in about 2 days." Article continues below Symptoms of norovirus. The NHS lists the primary symptoms of norovirus which usually begin suddenly and may include:. Article continues below You may also experience: How to treat norovirus at home. The NHS also outlines what steps to take should you or your child contract norovirus. It states: "You can usually treat it at home. You'll usually start to feel better in 2 to 3 days. Diarrhoea and vomiting can usually be treated at home. The most important thing is to have lots of fluids to avoid dehydration." Article continues below Ensure our latest health news always appears at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings. Do: Article continues below - remain at home and rest as much as possible. - drink plenty of fluids, such as water or squash – take small sips if you feel nauseous. Article continues below - continue breast or bottle feeding your baby – if they're being sick, try giving smaller feeds more frequently than usual. - give babies on formula or solid foods small sips of water between feeds. Article continues below - eat when you feel up to it – it may be worth steering clear of fatty or spicy foods. - take paracetamol if you're feeling uncomfortable – check the leaflet before giving it to your child. Article continues below Don't: - do not make baby formula weaker – use it at its usual strength. Article continues below - do not give children under 12 medicine to stop diarrhoea. - do not give aspirin to children under 16. analysis.time: The UKHSA issued the alert on 14 November 2026, with the current season's case count reported as of that date. The 48-hour stay-at-home guidance is applicable after symptoms cease, which typically last 2 days.
analysis.location_and_population: The alert is issued for the UK, specifically targeting the population in general, with a focus on areas where close contact is common, such as hospitals, care homes, schools, and nurseries.
analysis.event: The UKHSA issued a 48-hour 'stay at home' alert for individuals with symptoms of norovirus, emphasizing that hand sanitiser is ineffective against the virus. This is a public health advisory, not a confirmed outbreak.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The UKHSA reports 2,111 laboratory-confirmed cases during the current season, a 16.8% increase compared to the five-season average for the equivalent period. The virus spreads rapidly in close-contact environments, posing a risk of outbreaks.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The UKHSA has issued the alert and provided guidance on preventing the spread of norovirus, including self-isolation, hydration, and avoiding certain medications. The situation is under active monitoring, with no indication of resolution yet.

analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued a public health alert on 14 November 2026, urging individuals with norovirus symptoms to stay at home for 48 hours after their symptoms subside. This guidance is based on the agency's observation of a 16.8% rise in laboratory-confirmed cases during the current season compared to the five-season average. Norovirus, known as the winter vomiting bug, spreads rapidly in close-contact environments like hospitals, care homes, schools, and nurseries. The UKHSA warns that hand sanitiser is ineffective against the virus and advises people to avoid attending public places until 48 hours after symptoms stop. The agency also outlines home treatment measures, such as staying hydrated and avoiding certain medications, particularly for children. The alert reflects ongoing monitoring of the virus's spread and emphasizes the need for public adherence to isolation and hygiene protocols to mitigate further transmission.

news.content_zh: 英国健康安全局 (UKHSA) 于 2026 年 11 月 14 日发布公共卫生警报,敦促出现 诺如病毒 症状的个人在症状消退后留在家中 48 小时。该指南基于该机构的观察,即与五个季节的平均水平相比,本季节实验室确诊病例增加了 16.8%。诺如病毒,被称为冬季呕吐病,在医院、疗养院、学校和托儿所等密切接触环境中迅速传播。UKHSA 警告说,洗手液对病毒无效,并建议人们在症状停止 48 小时之前避免前往公共场所。该机构还概述了家庭 治疗 措施,例如保持水分和避免某些药物,特别是对于儿童。该警报反映了对病毒传播的持续监测,并强调公众需要遵守隔离和卫生协议,以进一步缓解 传播 的影响。

New figures show the number of people contracting norovirus has risen. Article continues below The UKHSA has taken to X, previously known as Twitter, to highlight a recent increase in cases of the bug. According to its data, 2,111 laboratory-confirmed infections have been recorded this season so far – marking a 16.8% rise compared to the five-season average for the equivalent timeframe. ‌ While figures remain within expected levels, the organisation has flagged that infections are climbing, with 257 reports logged during the fortnight leading up to last week. Guidance has been issued on the appropriate steps to take should symptoms emerge. View 2 Images People are advised to avoid fizzy drinks(Image: Getty) And one is two popular drinks that should be avoided. The NHS has advised that anyone with the bug should avoid fizzy drinks and fruit juice, as they can worsen a key symptom. What is norovirus? Often called the winter vomiting bug, norovirus can actually strike at any time of year. The stomach illness triggers vomiting and diarrhoea and transmits rapidly within communities, leading to frequent outbreaks in environments where people are in close proximity, including hospitals, care facilities, cruise liners, schools and nurseries. ‌ The virus targets the stomach and intestines and is also referred to as a gastrointestinal virus, gastric flu, or a stomach bug. It's possible to contract norovirus multiple times within a brief period, as various types (or genotypes) of the virus circulate simultaneously, reports the Mirror. While limited immunity may develop to one particular strain, infection from a different variant can occur shortly afterwards. Article continues below What should I do if I have it? The UKHSA has previously cautioned: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop as you are still infectious during this time." It also highlighted that hand sanitiser proves ineffective in preventing the illness. To halt the virus's spread, the health service advises those displaying symptoms to stay away from school, work, hospitals, and care homes for 48 hours following the cessation of symptoms. Beyond self-isolation while unwell, the NHS outlines various measures to contain the infection's transmission, recommending that you should: Article continues below Wash your hands with soap and water (alcohol hand gels do not kill norovirus) after using the toilet or changing nappies Wash your hands with soap and water before preparing, serving or eating food Wash clothes and bedding that has faeces or vomit on it at a 60C wash and separately from other laundry Clean toilet seats, flush handles, taps and bathroom door handles Avoid contact with others as much as possible If you exhibit any symptoms, the health body advises: Article continues below Do not go to school, nursery or work until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days Do not visit others in hospitals or places like care homes until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days If you or your child have diarrhoea for more than seven days or vomiting for more than two days, you should call 111. Article continues below According to the NHS, norovirus symptoms can emerge "suddenly" and typically comprise nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea. It notes: "It can be very unpleasant, but usually gets better in about 2 days." Symptoms of norovirus The NHS says the main symptoms of norovirus usually start suddenly and may include: Article continues below feeling sick being sick (vomiting) diarrhoea You may also have: Article continues below a high temperature a headache tummy pain body aches and pains How to treat norovirus yourself The NHS also explains what to do if you or your child have norovirus. It says: "You can usually treat it at home. You'll usually start to feel better in 2 to 3 days. Diarrhoea and vomiting can usually be treated at home. The most important thing is to have lots of fluids to avoid dehydration." Article continues below Ensure our latest health news always appears at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings Do: Article continues below stay at home and get plenty of rest drink lots of fluids, such as water or squash – take small sips if you feel sick carry on breast or bottle feeding your baby – if they're being sick, try giving small feeds more often than usual give babies on formula or solid foods small sips of water between feeds eat when you feel able to – it may help to avoid foods that are fatty or spicy take paracetamol if you're in discomfort – check the leaflet before giving it to your child Don't: Article continues below do not have fruit juice or fizzy drinks – they can make diarrhoea worse do not make baby formula weaker – use it at its usual strength do not give children under 12 medicine to stop diarrhoea do not give aspirin to children under 16 GET MORE FROM US Choose Liverpool Echo as a 'Preferred Source' on Google News for quick access to the news you value. analysis.brief_en: The NHS has issued warnings advising people to avoid fizzy drinks and fruit juice if they are infected with norovirus, as these can worsen symptoms. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported a 16.8% increase in laboratory-confirmed norovirus infections this season compared to the five-season average, with 257 cases logged in the fortnight leading up to November 14, 2026. Norovirus, often referred to as the winter vomiting bug, causes sudden symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea, typically resolving within two days. The guidance emphasizes self-isolation for 48 hours after symptoms subside, thorough handwashing with soap and water, and avoiding contact with others to prevent transmission. The NHS also recommends staying hydrated and avoiding certain foods, while noting that alcohol-based hand gels are ineffective against the virus. This advice is part of broader public health measures to manage the spread of norovirus, which is highly infectious and commonly found in communal settings.

news.content_title: GI Illness Outbreak Sickens 148 People on Caribbean Princess — Fourth Princess Cruises Outbreak in 2026
news.content: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that 134 passengers and 14 crew members have reported being ill with a gastrointestinal (GI) illness on Princess Cruises’ Caribbean Princess . The total number of sick crew members and passengers may increase as the ship is still at sea until November 23, when it returns to Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. The outbreak was first reported to the CDC on November 15 and publicly reported on November 17. The causative agent of the outbreak is currently listed as unknown, which is typical when an outbreak is first reported. The CDC lists the predominant symptoms as vomiting and diarrhea. Norovirus is the most common cause of GI outbreaks on cruise ships, accounting for 18 of 23 and 5 of 10 CDC-reported GI outbreaks in 2025 and 2026, respectively. This is the second GI outbreak on the Caribbean Princess this year. The ship previously suffered a norovirus outbreak on its April 28 to May 11, 2026, voyage that sickened 160 people (145 passengers and 15 crew members). Princess Cruises’ Star Princess and Ruby Princess also suffered norovirus outbreaks this year, sickening 193 and 132 people, respectively. This brings the total number of reported GI illness cases aboard Princess Cruises’ ships to 633 in 2026, including 527 passengers and 106 crew members. Princess Cruises accounts for four of the ten CDC-reported GI outbreaks in 2026. Only Lindblad Expeditions has experienced as many CDC-reported outbreaks this year, with four outbreaks aboard its National Geographic Sea Bird between May and July. The CDC reports GI outbreaks as part of its Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP). The VSP monitors cruise ships as they return to American ports for potential outbreaks. The CDC publicly reports an outbreak if 3% or more of a ship’s passengers or crew members have GI symptoms. Currently, 4.6% of passengers and 1.2% of crew aboard the Caribbean Princess have been reported as sick. Princess Cruises has not responded to our request for comment regarding the outbreak as of the time of publication

It says there have been a total of 2,111 laboratory reports of people with the infection so far in the current season - an increase of 16.8% on the five season average for the same period. Article continues below While it still remains within expected levels, the agency has alerted people that the infection has begun to increase with 257 reports over the two weeks up to last week. And it has shared information of what people should do if they have any of the symptoms of the bug. Article continues below View 2 Images It can leave people feeling very unwell(Image: Getty) Norovirus is often dubbed the winter vomiting bug despite being able to catch it throughout the year. It is a stomach bug that causes vomiting and diarrhoea that spreads easily through communities, making outbreaks common in settings where individuals have close contact such as hospitals, care homes, cruise ships, schools and nurseries. The virus infects the stomach and intestines, and is also known as a gastrointestinal virus, gastric flu or a stomach bug. You can catch norovirus more than once in a short time period because multiple types (or genotypes) of norovirus circulate at any given time and while you may develop limited immunity to one strain you can still be infected by a different one soon after. Article continues below View 2 Images There are seven potential symptoms(Image: Getty) The UKHSA previously warned: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop as you are still infectious during this time." It also warned at the time that hand sanitiser will not work to prevent the illness. Article continues below To prevent the virus's transmission, the health service recommends those experiencing symptoms should avoid attending school, work, hospitals, and care homes until 48 hours after the symptoms have ended. Apart from self-isolating whilst feeling unwell, the NHS sets out several steps to limit the infection's spread, suggesting that you should: Wash your hands with soap and water (alcohol hand gels do not kill norovirus) after using the toilet or changing nappies Wash your hands with soap and water before preparing, serving or eating food Wash clothes and bedding that has faeces or vomit on it at a 60C wash and separately from other laundry Clean toilet seats, flush handles, taps and bathroom door handles Avoid contact with others as much as possible Article continues below If you exhibit any symptoms, the health body advises: Do not go to school, nursery or work until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days Do not visit others in hospitals or places like care homes until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days Article continues below If you or your child have diarrhoea for more than seven days or vomiting for more than two days, you should call 111. Article continues below According to the NHS norovirus symptoms can appear "suddenly" and usually include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea. It adds: "It can be very unpleasant, but usually gets better in about 2 days." Symptoms of norovirus The NHS says the main symptoms of norovirus usually start suddenly and may include: Article continues below feeling sick being sick (vomiting) diarrhoea You may also have: Article continues below a high temperature a headache tummy pain body aches and pains How to treat norovirus yourself The NHS also explains what to do if you or your child have norovirus. It says: "You can usually treat it at home. You'll usually start to feel better in 2 to 3 days. Diarrhoea and vomiting can usually be treated at home. The most important thing is to have lots of fluids to avoid dehydration." analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued an urgent 48-hour 'stay at home' warning for anyone with symptoms of norovirus, as the infection has begun to increase. This advice was published on 14 November 2026 by The Mirror, a UK news outlet. The UKHSA reported 2,111 laboratory cases in the current season, a 16.8% rise compared to the five-season average for the same period. Over the two weeks up to last week, there were 257 reports, indicating a growing trend. The agency emphasized that hand sanitiser is ineffective against norovirus and that individuals should avoid attending school, work, hospitals, and care homes until 48 hours after symptoms subside. The NHS also provided guidance on preventing transmission, including thorough handwashing with soap and water, cleaning contaminated surfaces, and isolating to avoid spreading the virus. The situation is under active monitoring, and the advice is based on current data. Norovirus, often called the winter vomiting bug, is highly infectious and spreads easily in close-contact environments such as hospitals, care homes, cruise ships, schools, and nurseries. The virus infects the stomach and intestines and is known as a gastrointestinal virus. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea, which typically last about two days. The advice aims to reduce the spread of the virus and protect vulnerable populations.

news.source_body_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued an urgent 48-hour 'stay at home' warning for anyone with symptoms of norovirus, as the infection has begun to increase. This advice was published on 14 November 2026 by The Mirror, a UK news outlet. The UKHSA reported 2,111 laboratory cases in the current season, a 16.8% rise compared to the five-season average for the same period. Over the two weeks up to last week, there were 257 reports, indicating a growing trend. The agency emphasized that hand sanitiser is ineffective against norovirus and that individuals should avoid attending school, work, hospitals, and care homes until 48 hours after symptoms subside. The NHS also provided guidance on preventing transmission, including thorough handwashing with soap and water, cleaning contaminated surfaces, and isolating to avoid spreading the virus. The situation is under active monitoring, and the advice is based on current data. Norovirus, often called the winter vomiting bug, is highly infectious and spreads easily in close-contact environments such as hospitals, care homes, cruise ships, schools, and nurseries. The virus infects the stomach and intestines and is known as a gastrointestinal virus. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhoea, which typically last about two days. The advice aims to reduce the spread of the virus and protect vulnerable populations.

Elaine Blackburne Network Content Editor and Kate Lally Content Editor 13:19, 14 Nov 2026 View Image It can cause some grim symptoms(Image: SimpleImages via Getty Images) Health experts have urged against consuming two drinks if you fall ill with what's known as the 'winter vomiting bug', as they can exacerbate a primary symptom. Article continues below Powered By Scottish magician escapes straitjacket on bungee jump off bridge in Houdini tribute Share Next Stay Recent statistics reveal a norovirus cases have risen, although the number of people unwell is typical for this time of year. The NHS recommends that anyone suffering from the bug should avoid fizzy drinks and fruit juice, as they can aggravate a key symptom. ‌ Although it is known as the winter vomiting bug, norovirus can occur throughout the year. The stomach illness causes vomiting and diarrhoea and spreads quickly within communities, resulting in regular outbreaks in settings where individuals are in close contact, such as hospitals, care homes, cruise ships, schools and nurseries. The virus attacks the stomach and intestines and is commonly known as a gastrointestinal virus, gastric flu, or a stomach bug. It's possible to catch norovirus several times in a short space of time, as different types (or genotypes) of the virus are in circulation at the same time. Ensure our latest health news always appears at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as Preferred Source in your Google search settings While some immunity may be built up against one specific strain, you can be infected by another variant soon after. Among its lengthy advice, the NHS says to avoid fruit juice and fizzy drinks, as these can make diarrhoea worse. ‌ What should I do if I have norovirus? The UKHSA has previously warned: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop as you are still infectious during this time." It also stressed that hand sanitiser is ineffective at preventing the illness. To prevent the virus from spreading, the health service recommends that those with symptoms avoid school, work, hospitals, and care homes for 48 hours after symptoms have stopped. In addition to self-isolating while ill, the NHS has outlined several steps to help stop the infection spreading, advising that you should:. Article continues below If you show any symptoms, the health body recommends that you: Wash your hands with soap and water (alcohol hand gels do not kill norovirus) after using the toilet or changing nappies Avoid contact with others as much as possible Wash clothes and bedding that has faeces or vomit on it at a 60C wash and separately from other laundry Wash your hands with soap and water before preparing, serving or eating food Clean toilet seats, flush handles, taps and bathroom door handles Do not go to school, nursery or work until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days Do not visit others in hospitals or places like care homes until you have not been sick or had diarrhoea for two days Article continues below Should you or your child experience diarrhoea for longer than seven days or vomiting for more than two days, you should ring 111. According to the NHS, norovirus symptoms can appear "suddenly" and usually include feeling sick, being sick, and diarrhoea. It notes: "It can be very unpleasant, but usually gets better in about 2 days." Article continues below Symptoms of norovirus The NHS states the primary symptoms of norovirus typically begin abruptly and may include: feeling sick being sick (vomiting) diarrhoea Article continues below You may also experience a high temperature a headache tummy pain body aches and pains Article continues below NHS advice continues: "You can usually treat it at home. You'll usually start to feel better in 2 to 3 days. Diarrhoea and vomiting can usually be treated at home. The most important thing is to have lots of fluids to avoid dehydration." By Monica Torres Senior Reporter, Work/Life, Tech and General Lifestyle Nov 13, 2026, 07:00 AM EST |Updated Nov 13, 2026 View Comments LOADINGERROR LOADING 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Hand sanitizer is the first line of defense against sniffles and sneezes –– but infectious disease experts say people can put too much trust in its capabilities. “Most of your common viruses like influenza, COVID virus, they’re wimps. They’re easy to kill with hand sanitizer,” said Chuck Gerba, a microbiologist at the University of Arizona. He noted that these viruses have a fatty layer that soap and standard disinfectants can dissolve. Advertisement However, although alcohol-based hand sanitizer can inactivate other viruses like COVID, “norovirus doesn’t have a lipid layer and it’s much tougher to kill,” Gerba said. That’s why alcohol-based hand sanitizers are not effective against norovirus, or as Thomas Russo, an infectious disease expert and distinguished professor of medicine at the University at Buffalo, dubbed it: the “winter vomiting disease,” named after its hallmark symptoms. Since norovirus can live on surfaces for two weeks, hand hygiene is critical –– but you need to know which cleaning method is best for reducing your transmission risk, experts say. Advertisement Getty Hand sanitizer is a first line of defense but it isn't a cure-all against all winter viruses. Norovirus cases surge in the winter months, Russo said. He cited how viral survival favors cold, dry weather, and indoor crowds and holiday travel increases person-to-person contact. Moreover, there is no vaccine immunity from norovirus. Russo noted there are vaccines for common winter viruses like influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and COVID, but there is no shot for norovirus at this time, so people are more vulnerable to catching it. Although rare, 900 U.S. adults who were mostly ages 65 and older even die from norovirus every year. Advertisement “Norovirus is not inactivated by the alcohol-based sanitizers,” Russo said, so his recommendation for preventing the illness is vigorous hand washing with soap for at least 20 seconds, which will inactivate the virus and remove the particles from your skin. Alcohol-based hand sanitizers do kill flu, measles and COVID viruses, but Russo also notes that the main method of transmission of these viruses is through the air. Measles is back in the U.S., and “measles is really good with aerosols and can remain lingering in the air for up to two hours after someone that’s infected has left that closed space,” he said as an example. It’s one more reason you should not assume one kind of hand hygiene is enough to protect your health this winter. Too many people think “as long as I have good hand hygiene, it’s all good, and I’m not going to get infected,” Russo said. To avoid this fate, vaccinate yourself against respiratory viruses, and consider using both hand-washing and hand sanitizer to keep viruses from spreading. Advertisement “You can use hand sanitizers in addition to hand washing, but hand sanitizer is not a substitute for handwashing, which is best” against norovirus, according to the Centers for Disease Control. Take it from the professionals, who recommended using both when you suspect you may get sick from a winter virus. Gerba said in shopping malls and on cruise ships, he will often wash his hands with soap and water, and also use Advanced Purell hand sanitizer, which contains the CDC-recommended level of at least 60% alcohol, to cover all his bases. Gerba cited a 2024 study he co-authored, which found that using an automatic-dispensing hand sanitizer after using a public restroom significantly reduced the chances of getting norovirus and COVID. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported 2,111 laboratory cases so far this season – up 16.8% on the five-season average for the same period. While still within expected levels, 257 cases were recorded in just the two weeks to last week. Known as the winter vomiting bug, norovirus causes sudden nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea and spreads easily in places such as hospitals, schools and care homes. Crucially, the UKHSA has warned that hand sanitiser will not kill the virus. The agency previously warned: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop as you are still infectious during this time." Those with symptoms should also avoid work, school, hospitals and care homes until fully clear. The NHS says most cases can be treated at home by resting and drinking plenty of fluids, but advises calling 111 if diarrhoea lasts more than seven days or vomiting persists for more than two days. analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued an urgent alert regarding the rise in norovirus cases, urging individuals with seven specific symptoms to stay at home for 48 hours after they subside. This is due to the virus's high contagiousness, as people can still be infectious during this period. The UKHSA reported 2,111 laboratory cases this season, a 16.8% increase compared to the five-season average for the same period. While still within expected levels, 257 cases were recorded in the two weeks to last week. The agency emphasized that hand sanitiser is ineffective against norovirus and advised avoiding work, school, hospitals, and care homes until fully recovered. The NHS recommends home treatment for most cases, with advice to call 111 if symptoms persist beyond seven days for diarrhoea or two days for vomiting. This guidance aims to reduce the spread of the virus, particularly in high-risk environments such as hospitals and schools.

analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has issued a 'stay at home warning' as cases of norovirus, a highly contagious winter bug, have risen over recent weeks. The agency advises individuals with symptoms to remain at home for 48 hours after they have stopped to prevent further spread. According to data, there have been 2,111 laboratory reports of norovirus infections in the current season, marking a 16.8% increase compared to the previous season's average for the same period. The NHS notes that symptoms typically appear 12 to 48 hours after exposure and last about two to three days. It also highlights that hand sanitiser is ineffective in preventing the virus. The UKHSA previously warned that norovirus remains infectious for 48 hours after symptoms cease, reinforcing the need for isolation. The virus causes sudden inflammation of the stomach and intestines, leading to vomiting and diarrhoea, and is spread easily through direct contact and contaminated surfaces. The health authorities recommend avoiding school, nursery, work, and visits to hospitals or care homes until two days have passed without symptoms.

In terms of symptoms, reports of the vomiting bug were 40.4% higher during the period from October 26 to November 8. Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT The bug has started to spread quickly, with 257 reports over the two weeks up to last week, the health agency has said. The NHS says that symptoms usually appear 12 to 48 hours after exposure and last for roughly two to three days. Norovirus is easily spread from person to person. People can become infected through direct contact and touching contaminated surfaces. The NHS says norovirus can be "very unpleasant". Meanwhile, the UKHSA warns: "Norovirus is incredibly infectious, so if you're feeling unwell, stay home for 48 hours after symptoms stop, as you are still infectious during this time." Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Diarrhoea and vomiting are among the most common symptoms, and they can usually be treated at home. According to the NHS, there are three main symptoms of norovirus that usually start suddenly. They are: Vomiting Feeling sick Diarrhoea Symptoms can also include: a high temperature a headache tummy pain body aches and pains You can get norovirus at any time of the year, but it is most common in winter. If you or a child gets norovirus, it can usually be treated at home. One of the most important things to know about norovirus is how easily it spreads. People who contract the virus are urged to stay home until they recover. Norovirus is easily spread (Image: Getty) How to treat norovirus The NHS lists six steps to take to recover from norovirus. The advice is as follows: Stay at home and get plenty of rest Drink lots of fluids, such as water or squash – take small sips if you feel sick Carry on breast or bottle feeding your baby – if they're being sick, try giving small feeds more often than usual Give babies on formula or solid foods small sips of water between feeds Eat when you feel able to – it could help to stay away from foods that are fatty or spicy Take paracetamol if you're in discomfort – check the leaflet before giving it to your child Additionally, you should avoid fruit juice or fizzy drinks as they can make diarrhoea worse. Additionally, you should not make baby formula weaker, and do not give children under 12 medicine to stop diarrhoea, or give aspirin to children under 16. According to the NHS, there are three main symptoms of norovirus that usually start suddenly. They are: Vomiting Feeling sick Diarrhoea Symptoms can also include: a high temperature a headache tummy pain body aches and pains You can get norovirus at any time of the year, but it is most common in winter. If you or a child gets norovirus, it can usually be treated at home. One of the most important things to know about norovirus is how easily it spreads. People who contract the virus are urged to stay home until they recover. Norovirus is easily spread (Image: Getty) How to treat norovirus The NHS lists six steps to take to recover from norovirus. The advice is as follows: Stay at home and get plenty of rest Drink lots of fluids, such as water or squash – take small sips if you feel sick Carry on breast or bottle feeding your baby – if they're being sick, try giving small feeds more often than usual Give babies on formula or solid foods small sips of water between feeds Eat when you feel able to – it could help to stay away from foods that are fatty or spicy Take paracetamol if you're in discomfort – check the leaflet before giving it to your child Additionally, you should avoid fruit juice or fizzy drinks as they can make diarrhoea worse. Additionally, you should not make baby formula weaker, and do not give children under 12 medicine to stop diarrhoea, or give aspirin to children under 16. supplementary_news.content: AI Automated Translation. Font Size A A A A A Share AI Automated Translation. Stock Finance Industry Living Economy Tech Future theBio Entertainment Norovirus cases double as outbreak continues among young children, health agency warns Home > theBio Norovirus cases double as outbreak continues among young children, health agency warns By Hong Hyojin Updated Nov 17, 2026, 5:23 p.m. KST Published Nov 17, 2026, 5:11 p.m. KST Number of domestic norovirus infection cases / Graphic by Yoon Sun-jung The number of domestic norovirus infection patients has more than doubled over the past five years. In particular, as the rate of cluster outbreaks in kindergartens and daycare centers has risen, authorities have urged enhanced hygiene management within infant and toddler facilities, as well as improved personal hygiene practices. According to the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency’s (KDCA) sample surveillance system on Tuesday, the total number of norovirus infection patients reported this year through that date stood at 10,754, an increase of approximately 2.6 times compared with 2021 (4,082 cases). Notably, cluster outbreaks are occurring at high rates among infants and young children, who have recently emerged as a key vulnerable group for infection. According to KDCA statistics, the number of norovirus patients aged 0 to 6 rose by 89%, from 2,431 in 2021 to 4,601 as of Week 45 (the 1st–7) of 2026. A KDCA official stated, “Analysis of outbreak causes revealed that person-to-person transmission occurred in 88.5% of infant and toddler facilities between 2023 and 2025, identifying this as a major risk factor.” The official added, “Alongside public awareness campaigns on preventive guidelines, we plan to produce promotional videos explaining transmission routes and disinfection methods to guide childcare facilities. We also intend to coordinate with relevant government ministries to utilize these materials in training for childcare facility staff.” Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastrointestinal infections during the winter season. The primary infection routes include consuming raw seafood or food prepared by contaminated hands. Person-to-person transmission through direct contact with infected individuals is also possible, with the highest infectivity occurring 2 to 5 days after symptom onset. Infants and young children, who have weakened immunity, may experience repeated vomiting and diarrhea upon infection, leading to a rapid loss of body fluids. If a significant portion of body fluids is lost, the heart and kidneys can be damaged. Among infectious disease experts, there are also indications that infection transmission is not being properly controlled. Professor Eom Jung-sik, an infectious disease specialist at Gachon University Gil Hospital, said, “Given that a steady increase has been confirmed among infants and young children, who have relatively little exposure to shellfish consumption, it appears that issues are recurring in food distribution channels related to daycare or school meals.” He added, “It seems there is a problem within the traditional (transmission) chain of foodborne infectious diseases, such as contamination occurring during the supply and preparation of ingredients. In effect, infection control is not functioning.” Choi Yong-jae, president of the Korean Association of Pediatric and Adolescent Hospitals, said, “Even from our perspective in medical practice, we are seeing an increase in norovirus infection cases among children recently.” He added, “To block transmission, the best course of action is to strictly adhere to relevant hygiene guidelines, such as handwashing and thoroughly cooking food.” Norovirus is highly transmissible, capable of causing infection with even a small amount of the virus, and exhibits high resistance, surviving at temperatures as low as -20°C. It does not easily die off under standard cooking temperatures, tap water chlorine concentrations, or surface cleaning agents. The virus can be excreted through feces for up to two weeks after symptoms disappear, necessitating caution even after recovery. To prevent infection, food should be cooked until it reaches a core temperature of 85°C for at least one minute before consumption, and hygiene guidelines such as handwashing and disinfecting kitchen utensils must be strictly followed. If symptoms have already appeared, patients should seek diagnosis from a specialist to accurately assess their condition and receive intravenous fluid treatment if dehydration is severe. Antidiarrheal medications that suppress diarrhea should be avoided as much as possible, as they can hinder the elimination of toxins. A KDCA official said, “Since infants and young children find it difficult to maintain personal hygiene on their own, we ask parents and teachers to guide them in practicing proper handwashing in daily life.” The official added, “We also urge attention to hygiene management, including disinfection within infant and toddler facilities.” "This article was translated using AI and may differ slightly from the original." 1.
